deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This is a station adjustment (Stationsausgleichung) for the station Jever. The neighbouring stations (Aurich, Witmund, Dornum, Esens, Wangeroog, Langwarden, Varel, Bremerlehe, Brillit, Zeven) belong to the north-west German / Hannover–Oldenburg triangulation. So, despite the bundle label '1813', this sheet is almost certainly from the late 1820s or 1830s; that dating is my inference. The previous and next pages treat Langwarden and Brillit in exactly the same way.

(A) PROVISIONAL DIRECTIONS AND REDUCTION TO THE CENTRE.
- Directions (in degrees, minutes and seconds, ° ' ") are listed to:
  1 Aurich 69°39'17.200
  2 Witmund 95°0'42.221 + a
  3 Dornum 107°2'27.863
  4 Esens 115°22'28.363 + b
  5 Wangeroog 173°35'13.377 + c
  6 Langwarden 263°59'56.719 + d
  7 Varel 322°58'20.546 + e
- a,…,e are the unknown corrections. Aurich and Dornum get no unknown: each occurs in only one angle (1.2 and 3.4), so each simply follows its partner direction.
- Column 'Red. auf das C.' (= reduction to the centre): corrections +7.224", −40.217", −57.100", +51.015" are applied. This gives reduced directions 69°39'24.424, 115°21'48.146, 173°34'16.277, 322°59'11.561.
- The marginal note '259°18'28", 6.772, Halbm. 7.012 / 7.057' plausibly gives the centring elements: the direction of the centre, the eccentric distance, and two measured radii (Halbmesser) of the tower. This is my interpretation.

(B) TRIAL RESECTION.
- For four reduced directions an orientation constant (azimuth from coordinates minus direction) is formed, linearised in the station coordinates:
  O1 = 1°38'48.907 + 6.385 dx − 2.367 dy
  O2 = 53.164 + 8.896 dx + 4.217 dy
  O3 = 47.004 + 0.940 dx + 8.344 dy
  O4 = 37.828 − 4.990 dx − 6.618 dy
- Trial dx = −0.88, dy = −0.29 gives 43.974, 44.113, 43.757, 44.138 (spread 0.38").
- Trial dx = −0.94, dy = −0.31 gives 43.639, 43.495, 43.530, 44.570 (spread 1.07"). So the first trial is the better one.
- In other words, the station position is fixed by making the orientation constants agree: resection by differential corrections.

(C) FIRST ADJUSTMENT (no systematic term).
- Each angle i.j has a weight w, with its split (e.g. 12 = 12+0, 40 = 20+20) and its mean value.
- The error equation is v = (provisional direction_j − provisional direction_i − measured angle) + (unknown_j − unknown_i).
  Example, 2.4: 20°21'46.142 − 46.675 = −0.533, so v = −0.533 − a + b.
- The remaining constants are +0.323, +0.040, +0.181, +0.180, −0.175, +0.093, −0.262, +0.642.
- Angles 1.2 and 3.4 have zero residual and are omitted.
- Normal equations [w·coef·coef] and [w·coef·n]:
  +0.008 + 34a − 10b − 6c − 6d − 12e
  +0.004 − 10a + 26b − 6c − 10e
  +0.024 − 6a − 6b + 76c − 40d − 24e
  0 − 6a − 40c + 126d − 80e
  −0.036 − 12a − 10b − 24c − 80d + 126e
- All rows of the matrix sum to zero; the system is singular because only direction differences enter. The constants are about 0, so the provisional directions are already essentially the least-squares solution.

(D) SECOND ADJUSTMENT WITH A CONSTANT ANGLE ERROR x*.
- Each angle is separated into its 'direct' part and its 'supplement' (360°-complement) part.
  - Direct part (marked +): true angle = observed + x*.
  - Supplement part (marked −): true angle = observed − x*.
  - Mixed series get no x.
- Put x* = 0.381" + x. The new provisional directions are 69°39'17.167, 95°0'42.188, 115°22'28.343, 173°35'13.354, 263°59'56.725, 322°58'20.541.
- Example, 2.4 direct, weight 5, 46.200: 46.155 − 46.200 − 0.381 = −0.426, so v = −0.426 − a + b − x.
- Example, 2.4 supplement, weight 5, 47.150: 46.155 − 47.150 + 0.381 = −0.614, so v = −0.614 − a + b + x.
- The same treatment is applied to 2.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.7 and 7.2. The weighted means of the parts reproduce the means of section (C).
- Normal equations:
  −0.028 + 168x + 2a + 4c − 6d
  −0.002 + 2x + 34a − 10b − 6c − 6d − 12e
  +0.002 − 10a + 26b − 6c − 10e
  +0.002 + 4x − 6a − 6b + 76c − 40d − 24e
  +0.012 − 6x − 6a − 40c + 126d − 80e
  −0.014 − 12a − 10b − 24c − 80d + 126e
  All constants are about 0, so x* ≈ +0.381" is the adjusted value.
- Weight of x* after eliminating a,…,e: P = 168 − gᵀM⁻¹g = 167.4926, with g = (2,0,4,−6) and M the a–d block (fixing e = 0 is my choice; any one unknown may be fixed).
- Sum of squares 14.734424; divided by 10 gives 1.4734424; its square root m = 1.2138543" is the mean error of unit weight.
- E.m. of x* = m/√P = 0.094". E.v. (probable error) is given as 0.065".
errors: Line 2.6, weight 4, value 14.812: the constant must be −0.275, not +0.275. Check: 168°59'14.537 − 14.812 = −0.275. The [a] and [d] normal-equation constants (−0.002, +0.012) are reproduced only with −0.275. The '+x' on this line is struck out, and the [xx] = 168 count confirms this sub-series carries no x.
Line 7.2 direct: recomputation gives −0.276 against the written −0.277. This is a rounding difference, probably from x* being carried to more decimals.
E.v. 0.065": the usual probable error 0.6745 × 0.0938 = 0.063". The written figure is slightly high (minor slip or a different factor).
Sum of squares 14.734 cannot be reproduced from the residuals on the page: Σw·v² of the 16 equations in (D) is ≈ 12.01. It may include data not shown here (e.g. scatter within the series).

Divisor 10: with 16 equations and 5 independent unknowns (4 independent direction corrections plus x, the a–e block being singular) one would expect 11. Gauss seems to count a–e as 5 independent unknowns. This is a possible off-by-one, unless further observations not shown on the page are included.

results.what: Station adjustment of observed angles to directions by least squares with weights, normal equations and a singular system (directions defined up to a constant)
results.modern_name: Least-squares station adjustment (method of directions / Gauss–Markov model)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (least squares 1795/1809/1821–23; station adjustment in the Hannover Gradmessung)

results.what: Extra unknown x* for a constant systematic error between direct angles and their supplements (360° complements), with its weight 167.49 and mean error 0.094"
results.modern_name: Least-squares estimation of a systematic (bias) parameter / additional-parameter adjustment
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Hannover triangulation practice); later Bessel, Gerling, Helmert

results.what: Reduction of eccentric directions to the centre, and fixing of station coordinates by linearised orientation constants with trial dx, dy
results.modern_name: Centring reduction and resection by differential corrections
results.usually_credited_to: Standard geodetic practice (Snellius/Pothenot problem; differential form in Gauss's time)

results.what: Mean error of unit weight m = sqrt(Σwvv/(n−u)) and mean error of an unknown m/√P; probable error ≈ 0.6745 m
results.modern_name: A-posteriori standard deviation and parameter standard error

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working computation from Gauss's triangulation practice. The constant direct/supplement error term is a known feature of his station adjustments in the Hannover survey. Nothing goes beyond his published methods.

checkable.asserts: Constant of the first normal equation in the first adjustment
Constant of the e-equation (−0.036) in the first adjustment
The split 2.6 values reproduce the mean 168°59'14.458
The split 5.6 values reproduce the mean 90°24'43.162
Constant −0.028 of the x normal equation
Constant −0.002 of the a normal equation, which requires −0.275 on line 2.6
Weight of x* after eliminating the direction unknowns (e fixed at 0)
Weighted sum of squares of the residuals on the page is about 12.01, not the 14.734 written

transcription_corrections: 'Red. auf das 6.' is almost certainly 'Red. auf das C.' (Centrum), i.e. reduction to the centre; compare 'R. ad Centr.' on the next page.
Line 2.6, weight 4: read '14,812' with the constant '−0,275' (not +0,275); the '+x' at the end is struck out.
'E.v.' is the probable error (wahrscheinlicher Fehler) and 'E.m.' the mean error (mittlerer Fehler).
In the a-equation of the second normal system the term is '+34a' (the transcription's '+34a' is correct; it is written over '−').
